subject: MSA + Order Form DPA — SCCs exhibit and processor responsibilities clarification
messages:
From: Anna Patel <anna@horizonhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-01T08:15:00Z
Subject: MSA + Order Form DPA: SCCs exhibit and processor responsibilities

Mateo — attaching our redlines to the DPA and the Order Form. We have two items we need you to confirm: (1) the SCCs exhibit currently lists Redwood as ‘Processor’ with a paragraph saying Horizon will be Controller for patient data — we want explicit language that limits Redwood’s use to inference-only and prohibits model retraining on customer data, and (2) your subprocessors exhibit is blank; procurement needs a clear list or a binding commitment to notify and allow objection for any EU-resident subprocessors.

High level asks: 
- Can you confirm if Redwood’s proposed SCCs exhibit covers the export paths for EU data? We need to avoid any US-to-EU backflow unless adequately covered by SCCs + transfer impact addenda.
- Please send the latest track-changed DPA (with SCCs) and a one-page processor responsibilities summary we can put in our legal queue.

We’d like to close contracting by 2028-06-10 to meet procurement timelines.

Thanks,
Anna Patel
Associate GC, Horizon Health
[Attachment: Horizon_DPA_Redlines_20280601.pdf (pdf)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form DPA: SCCs exhibit and processor responsibilities

Hi Anna — thanks for the detailed redlines. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (privacy/ops) — see the attachments I’m sending: our current DPA with SCCs exhibit (Redwood_DPA_SCCs_v2) and a one-page summary of processor responsibilities.

Quick answers up front: 
- We will not use customer data to retrain foundation models — we can add an explicit non-retraining clause under Section 2.c of the DPA.
- Subprocessor disclosure: we will provide the current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days’ notice before onboarding any new EU-resident subprocessor; we can accept a procurement-style objection process limited to bona fide data-locality/security reasons.
- Export paths: our SCCs exhibit plus a short transfer impact addendum (TIA) will document cross-border flows. For customers requiring data-at-rest in EU only, we can offer a deployment scoping note (Private deployment or dedicated EU tenancy).

Milestone proposal: 
1) Karthik to provide specific alternative language for processor/subprocessor clauses by EOD 2028-06-01.
2) We’ll send a combined tracked DPA (Redwood + Horizon changes) by 2028-06-02.
3) Final signatures by 2028-06-09 to meet your procurement ask.

Anna — is the procurement review limited to legal, or do your security and compliance teams need to review the TIA as well? If so, please share a contact.

Thanks — Mateo
Director, Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_SCCs_v2.docx (docx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anna Patel <anna@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form DPA: SCCs exhibit and processor responsibilities

On 2028-06-01 10:02, Mateo Alvarez wrote:
> Looping in Karthik (legal) and Laura (privacy/ops) — see the attachments I’m sending...

Thanks — read the redlines. I drafted targeted alternative language (see attached) but flag two negotiation points you should expect:

1) Non-retraining clause — acceptable, but we need a carveout for model safety improvements that do not retain customer-identifiable inputs (propose: "processing of aggregated, de-identified telemetry for system safety only").

2) Subprocessor objection window — we can commit to 30 days’ notice and an objection process limited to demonstrable regulatory or technical reasons. We’ll resist open-ended veto rights.

Suggested edits (high level):
- Replace current Section 5.2 with: "Processor shall maintain a current list of Subprocessors and shall provide Customer with written notice of any new Subprocessor at least 30 days prior to engagement. Customer may object on reasonable data-locality or regulatory grounds; the Parties will meet to resolve objections in good faith and, absent resolution, Processor may propose mitigation measures (e.g., EU-only tenancy) prior to termination rights taking effect."
- Add clause 2.c: "Processor will not use Customer Content to retrain or improve foundation models used for general public services; Processor may process aggregated, irreversibly de-identified telemetry for system safety and stability purposes, provided such processing does not permit re-identification of Customer Content."

Operational asks for Laura: can you confirm the current list of EU-resident subprocessors and whether we can provide a short attestation of encryption-at-rest for EU hostings?

I attached an annotated draft (KIyer_DPA_annotated.docx). Once Laura confirms the infra points, Mateo — send a consolidated tracked DPA to Anna.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: KIyer_DPA_annotated.docx (docx)]

From: Anna Patel <anna@horizonhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-03T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form DPA: SCCs exhibit and processor responsibilities

Mateo/Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Procurement confirms security (secops@horizonhealth.com) will also review the TIA — I copied contracts only for now but can loop security if you’d like.

Two quick confirmations from our side: 
1) The non-retraining language you propose is acceptable if the telemetry carveout is strictly non-identifiable and scoped to system safety. Please ensure the tracked draft reflects "irreversibly de-identified" and gives examples (latency metrics, aggregate token-distribution stats) rather than raw logs.
2) Subprocessor notice + 30-day window is acceptable; procurement asks that you include an initial list of subprocessors for EU hostings and an attestation that any new EU-resident subprocessor will either (a) be subject to SCCs or (b) be on a private tenancy.

Please send the combined tracked DPA with the KIyer edits incorporated and a short one-page TIA that maps export paths and options (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private). We will move the packet into our legal queue upon receipt.

Also attaching our SOC2 certificate for procurement records. Once we have the combined DPA, we will run DocuSign and prep an OOF for signature routing.

Anna
Associate GC, Horizon Health
